tasks.title: What a project can configure, and what reads it
tasks.prompt: I want to document everything a project can put in its own folder to change how kurtkode behaves: instruction files, settings files, and the folders it looks in for extensions. Go through the code (the Swift package in AgentCore/) and list every file or folder inside a project, not in the user's home folder, that kurtkode reads to configure itself, including the alternative names it accepts for compatibility with other tools. For each one, say what it configures and which source file reads it, with a path:line reference. Also say which of them can make kurtkode run commands outside its sandbox, and what kurtkode does about that before running them. Don't change any files.

answer.name: permission rules from the settings files
the user approves project hooks or servers first

tasks.title: When kurtkode offers to escalate a run
tasks.prompt: Users ask when and why kurtkode offers to hand a request over to a stronger model. From the code (AgentCore/ and App/), explain: every reason a main run can earn an escalation offer, covering the automatic ones, the ones that depend on a setting, and the ones the user triggers; which ways a run can end that deliberately don't count; which model the offer goes to; and what the offer card's actions are, in what order. Give a path:line reference for each reason. Don't change any files.

answer.name: a reply cut off at the output limit
its last check failed after changing files
the project's tests fail after the run
a delegated task's check fails when re-run

tasks.title: How spending limits stop a run
tasks.prompt: Explain how kurtkode keeps spending within the user's limits. From the code (AgentCore/ and App/): which spending limits exist and where the user sets each; what counts toward them, including subagents, summaries, local models, and remote models whose price kurtkode doesn't know; when the check happens; and what happens, and what the user can do, when a limit is reached. Give path:line references. Don't change any files.

answer.name: unpriced remote models count at $3/$15 a million
subagents count toward the same limits
the run stops at the limit
